lines.text: # One Foot Home
[Intro — Acoustic Guitar, Mandolin]
Four years old in Republic snow
Point that trike downhill and go
[Verse 1]
There was a little valley out behind the house
Sparse green timber and a world spread out
Scott built a jump in the downhill track
I’d hit that bump and land on my back
Snow down my collar, tears in my eyes
Not from the hurting, but wounded pride
Drag that trike uphill again
Certain this time I was gonna win
One dark evening I looked up north
A rectangle of white light flashed right forth
Nobody saw it, nobody knew
I just stood there wondering what passed through
[Pre-Chorus]
Maybe I was always that kid
Standing still while my questions ran
One foot planted where I belonged
One already looking beyond where I am
[Chorus]
I’ve always had one foot home
And one foot over the line
Loved every place that ever held me
Still wondered what I might find
Too tied to the people to leave ’em
Too curious ever to stay
I’ve spent my whole life loving where I’m standing
While looking a little farther away
[Verse 2]
Dad disappeared ten yards from home
Into solder smoke and an engineer’s zone
Circuit boards and prototype schemes
Oscilloscopes glowing over half-built dreams
I’d come find him just to sit nearby
He’d smile without looking up from the light
“Grab you something, keep yourself still”
So I learned how quiet a lonely room feels
I watched those hands make thought into things
Wire into answers, relays into wings
I wanted his time, but I learned his way
Sometimes love sits near you with nothing to say
[Instrumental Turn — Dobro]
[Verse 3]
Then summers came near Mineral way
Gravel roads getting smaller all day
Through the Christian camp, over the creek
Up through the timber where Grandma would be
Grandpa built mountains underneath that place
Block after block at a minister’s pace
Basement, family room, porch out front
Then a garage because apparently he wasn’t done
Grandma had needles and organ keys
Grandpa had scripture and engineering disease
And I had a creek full of fossilized stone
And hills big enough to climb on my own
Nine years old, that forest was wide
Every little ridge was the mountainside
Petrified wood in a muddy hand
Was treasure enough for a wealthy man
[Chorus]
I’ve always had one foot home
And one foot over the line
Loved every place that ever held me
Still wondered what I might find
Too tied to the people to leave ’em
Too curious ever to stay
I’ve spent my whole life loving where I’m standing
While looking a little farther away
[Verse 4]
Years later high in the Three Sisters air
On the back of a horse that could carry me anywhere
Alpine timber and meadow grass
Whole damn counties rolling past
There’s something about a powerful horse
That makes a man quit arguing with force
You point toward country too steep to fake
And trust four legs with every step they take
Up there the questions got wonderfully small
No need to answer the meaning of it all
Just leather creaking, wind through pine
And enough open country to borrow some time
[Bridge — Pull Back]
Mom saw something before I did
A world getting narrow around that kid
Maybe she feared what she couldn’t name
Maybe fear and love sometimes look the same
Dad and I found each other late
Not father and boy, but friend to mate
Enough good years to settle the score
Before life came kicking through one more door
And I don’t need to rewrite a thing
Not the empty rooms or the broken wings
Every road I thought might ruin the plan
Put another tool in the hands of the man
[Build]
The other day I thought about
That eight-year-old looking out
Trying to guess what a grown man was
And whether he’d ever measure up
And damn if it didn’t hit me strange
After all the miles and all the change
I became somebody he’d look up to
Hell...
I think he’d think I was cool
[Final Chorus]
I still keep one foot home
And one foot over the line
Still love the places that made me
Still wonder what I might find
I never got too big to need them
Never got small enough to stay
I’m still that kid with snow in his collar
Getting back up anyway
[Outro — Sparse]
Creek stones, solder smoke
Mountain trails and things unspoke
A flash of light in a northern sky
A boy asking how and a man asking why
One foot home
One foot gone
And somehow both
Keep pulling me on
